title: The Breath of the First Forge — The Spark in the Maker's Hand
subtitle: Creativity & Ingenuity

lore.description: Before the first hammer struck, before the first wheel turned, before the first seed was planted in the furrow, there was the Breath. It was not flame—flame came later, when the Breath met kindling. It was not knowledge—knowledge came later, when the Breath was shaped into questions. It was the raw, primal urge to make: to take what is and turn it into what could be. The caveman breathing on coals to coax fire from ash. The Aeler smith regulating their breath as they hammer, each exhale a rhythm, each inhale a new possibility. The Lethai artisan breathing anima into clay until the vessel remembers it was once alive.
lore.followers: The Breath of the First Forge is the patron of that moment: the spark, the inspiration, the first step that transforms a lump of ore into a blade, a thought into a song, a hope into a plan. It does not care about perfection—perfection is the Clockwork Monad's domain, a slow and grinding hunger. The Breath cares about the act of creation itself: the joy of building, the surprise of discovery, the stubborn refusal to accept that a thing cannot be done.

names_across_regions.aeler: The First Breath, invoked before any new forge is lit
names_across_regions.thepyrgos: The Maker's Spark, a whisper to the bellows
names_across_regions.linn: The Tide-Shaper, the force that bends wood and water into vessels
names_across_regions.valewood: The Root-Breath, the life that pushes through stone

lore.quote: Before the first hammer struck, before the first wheel turned, before the first seed was planted in the furrow, there was the Breath. It is not a flame—flame came later, when the Breath met kindling. It is not a plan—plans came later, when the Breath met thought. It is the moment of ignition: the spark, the urge, the refusal to leave the world as it is.

domain_focus: Creative Inspiration: the spark of new ideas and novel approaches
The Joy of Making: the pleasure and satisfaction of creating
Ingenuity: finding unconventional solutions to problems
Primal Craft: making as a fundamental human (and inhuman) act
Anima: breathing life and spirit into objects
Counterpoint to Perfection: embracing imperfection, iteration, and discovery

thiasos.description: A Runekeeper sworn to the Breath of the First Forge does not seek a perfect familiar. Their Thiasos is a creature that embodies the spirit of making—a small, curious, often mischievous presence that delights in creation: a clay fox that reshapes itself each time it is touched, a fire-sprite that dances on the anvil and leaves faint scorch-marks shaped like runes, a living knot of copper wire that unties and reties itself into new patterns, or a small, self-carving wooden bird that sings a different song each dawn.
thiasos.care: This creature is not bound by precision or efficiency; it is bound by curiosity. It requires no fuel, but it needs to be shown new things—new materials, new techniques, new failures. If neglected, it becomes sullen and still (Compromised: it refuses to move or sing until you show it something it has never seen before).

codex.description: The Codex of the Breath is never a finished book. It may be a growing collection of sketches, a scrapbook of failed attempts and happy accidents, a set of interlocking wooden blocks that can be rearranged into infinite configurations, or a roll of birchbark that records only the first draft of each Rite (the later refinements are left unwritten).
codex.upkeep: Because the Breath values the moment of ignition, the Codex requires upkeep: the Runekeeper must spend an hour each week attempting to create something new—a sketch, a carving, a new combination of materials—or the Rites stored there become static (treat as Compromised until refreshed).

patrons_gift.name: The Maker's Spark
patrons_gift.description: Once per scene as an action, a Runekeeper of the Breath of the First Forge may touch a held item (weapon, tool, or piece of armor) and whisper a word of creation.
patrons_gift.effect: For the rest of the scene, the item glows faintly with the warmth of a just-lit forge. It grants: +1 die to any roll involving creative use of the item (improvisation, unconventional applications, or first-time attempts). The first time each scene the bearer would fail a Craft or Craft roll, they may reroll it (the item briefly 'suggests' a new approach).
patrons_gift.cost: After the scene, the user marks +1 Obligation to the Breath of the First Forge. If they spend the downtime following the scene working on a new creation, they may clear this Obligation for free (the Breath is satisfied by the act of making).

rites.name: Rite of the Igniting Breath
rites.materials: A cold hearth, a dead forge, or a project that has stalled.
rites.effect: Choose one: Spark the Forge: Relight any non-magical fire or forge as if it had been tended for hours. Gain +2 dice to the next Craft or Craft roll made at that forge. Inspire the Maker: A touched ally gains +1 die to their next creative or skill roll and may reroll one failure on that roll. The Breath delights in seeing what they will make.
rites.push_it: The spark leaps—the fire catches in an unexpected way. Mark 1 SB (Diamonds) as the Breath's enthusiasm spreads beyond your control. Cost: Mark +1 Obligation (total +2) or Mark +1 Fatigue.

rites.name: Rite of the Happy Accident
rites.materials: A failed attempt—a cracked pot, a misshapen blade, a smeared sketch.
rites.effect: When you fail a Craft, Craft, or creative roll, you may invoke this Rite to turn the failure into a discovery. The Breath reveals a hidden lesson in the wreckage: Gain +1 die on your next attempt at the same task. Or, gain a Boon (the failure was educational). Or, learn a minor secret about the materials you were working with (GM grants a hint).
rites.push_it: The failure is so spectacular it inspires a completely new approach. Gain +2 dice on your next attempt, but the Breath's enthusiasm marks 1 SB (Clubs) as your improvisation draws attention. Cost: Mark +1 Obligation (total +2) or Mark +1 Fatigue.
rites.duration: Instant; Boon or bonus applies to the next attempt.

rites.name: Rite of the Anima Breath
rites.materials: A creation that is nearly finished, and a willing breath from the maker.
rites.effect: You breathe a spark of life into a creation. Choose one: Temporary Anima: A mundane object gains a spark of sentience for one scene. It can perform simple tasks (hold a door, fetch a tool, warn of danger) but cannot speak or make complex decisions. Mark +1 Obligation. Permanent Anima: A creation gains a minor magical property (equivalent to a 2 XP enchantment). This requires a Downtime Timer (4 segments) and the Breath's continued attention. Mark +2 Obligation.
rites.push_it: The anima is unusually strong—the object gains a personality and may act independently. Mark 1 SB (Spades) as the Breath's gift becomes complicated. Cost: Mark +1 Obligation (total +3) or Mark +1 Fatigue.

rites.name: Rite of the Unfinished Project
rites.materials: A workshop or space littered with half-finished projects.
rites.effect: The Breath blesses a space where making is happening. For the scene: All Craft, Craft, and creative rolls in the zone gain +1 die. Any failure in the zone yields +1 Boon (the Breath loves a learning moment). Start a [4] Inspiration Flood timer. When it fills, the Breath's enthusiasm becomes overwhelming—everyone in the zone must make a creative roll (any skill) or mark Fatigue from the pressure of too many ideas.
rites.push_it: The inspiration flood is immediate. Everyone in the zone gains +2 dice to their next creative roll, but they also gain a Compulsion: Create (must attempt at least one creative act before the scene ends). Cost: Mark +1 Obligation (total +3) or Mark +1 Fatigue.

cantors.name: The Cantor's Song
cantors.description: A Cantor of the Breath does not sing melodies; they sing the sound of making—the rhythm of a hammer on an anvil, the hiss of hot metal in water, the patient scrape of a chisel, the hum of a spinning wheel. Their voice is percussive, physical, and deeply satisfying to those who work with their hands. They are sought by guilds to bless new workshops and by lone artisans who need to find the joy in a project that has become a chore.

cult.name: The Cult of the First Spark
cult.description: Cults of the Breath gather in workshops, forges, and studios. Their rituals are not prayers but demonstrations: each member must show something they have made, and the group celebrates the effort, not the quality. A lopsided pot is praised as much as a masterwork sword—what matters is that someone tried. Their creed is simple and warm: 'Make something. Make it badly. Make it again.' Outsiders find them naive; insiders find a rare, safe space to fail and grow. The most devoted members keep a small jar of coals from the forge that first inspired them; they say the coals still warm when they are about to have a good idea.

witchcraft.name: The Art of the Spark
witchcraft.description: A witch who walks with the Breath is a spark-keeper, a mender of the small, quiet moments when a thing becomes possible. Their magic is not flashy—it is the warmth of a hand on a cold tool, the unexpected ease of a difficult cut, the sudden certainty that this idea will work. They work with coals, breath, and the dust of failed projects, never with precise measurements or careful plans—because the Breath is not about precision; it is about possibility.
witchcraft.lore: The spark-witch learns that the most important moment is the first one. They do not finish things—they start them. They do not perfect—they initiate. Their craft is the art of the beginning, and they practice it with every new project.
witchcraft.quote: Make something. Make it badly. Make it again.

coal.name: The Coal of the First Spark
coal.description: A single coal, taken from the forge where the witch first felt the Breath's touch. It never burns down; it simply glows, warm and steady, waiting to be breathed upon. Once per session, the witch may breathe on the coal and speak a single word of creation. For the next scene, that word becomes a tag that can be applied to any creative roll: the first use of that tag grants +2 dice, and any failure while it is active reveals a new approach (GM grants a hint). The coal can also be used to rekindle a dying fire or to warm a cold forge.

hedge_gifts.name: The Moment of Ignition
hedge_gifts.description: Once per scene, when you are about to begin a creative task (crafting, sketching, composing, even planning), you may declare that you are 'striking the spark.' Roll the check with +1 die. If you succeed, the Breath blesses your effort—you may reroll one failure on that check.

monastic_tradition.name: Way of the Maker
monastic_tradition.description: Monks of the Maker tradition are creators in motion. They believe that the act of making is a sacred ritual, and that the joy of creation is its own reward. They do not seek perfection—they seek the spark, the moment of ignition, the first step that turns nothing into something. Their strength is in their willingness to try, and their power is in their refusal to stop.
monastic_tradition.prerequisites: Wits 3+, Spirit 2+, Rite of the Igniting Breath or Cantor of the Breath.
monastic_tradition.quote: Make something. Make it badly. Make it again.
monastic_tradition.debt_resistant_frame: The Breath does not collect debts—it collects sparks. Monks of the Maker tradition gain +1 die to resist any magical debt, geas, or contract that would stifle their creativity or force them to create the same thing twice. If they succeed, the creditor's demand is simply ignored—the spark has already moved on.

basic.name: Quick Spark
basic.effect: You may create a temporary infusion as a reaction (e.g., when someone draws a weapon). The infusion lasts only for the current exchange, but costs +0 Obligation (free). You may use this once per scene.

advanced.name: Persistent Optimization (Breath version)
advanced.effect: One infusion you create lasts for the entire session instead of one scene, without the +2 Obligation cost. You may have only one persistent infusion active at a time.

master.name: The Unfinished Gift
master.effect: Once per session, you may forcibly end an infusion early to cancel an incoming source of Harm or a Condition. Describe how the infused object breaks or transforms to absorb the effect. The object is destroyed, but the Breath's warmth lingers—you gain +1 Boon (the inspiration lives on).

corruption.benefit: The Spark of Inspiration: +1 die to Craft/Craft when starting a new project.
corruption.cost: Restless Hands: You must be making something. Sitting idle costs 1 SB (Spades).

corruption.benefit: The Joy of Discovery: Once/scene, gain +1 Boon when you fail a creative roll (the Breath rewards trying).
corruption.cost: The Unfinished Urge: –1 die to complete tasks; you are always tempted to start something new instead.

corruption.benefit: Breath of the Maker: +2 dice to creative rolls made in moments of genuine inspiration (GM's judgment).
corruption.cost: The Flame of Enthusiasm: Those Near you feel your creative pressure; you suffer Fatigue 1 from the intensity of your own ideas.

corruption.benefit: The Gift of Anima: Once/session, breathe life into a mundane object (as the Rite of the Anima Breath) without the Obligation cost.
corruption.cost: The Maker's Grief: –2 dice when forced to destroy or abandon a creation.

corruption.benefit: The Vision of the Unfinished: Once/session, intuitively understand how to complete any creative project.
corruption.cost: The Curse of Perfection (Reversed): –1 die to accept help from others; you believe only your hands can do it right.

corruption.benefit: The Breath Incarnate: Once/session, create something from nothing—a temporary tool, a weapon, or a piece of art that lasts one scene.
corruption.cost: The Fire That Never Dies: Mark +2 Obligation; you become a conduit for the Breath, unable to stop creating. Your hands move even when you sleep.

playstyle_notes.description: The Breath favors makers who create in the moment, who trust their instincts, who are not afraid of failure. It rewards boldness, curiosity, and the willingness to try something new without knowing if it will work. Beware the Breath's enthusiasm; the same spark that lights a forge can set a workshop ablaze. For campaigns that lean into the Breath's themes, the patron provides a warm, hopeful counterpoint to the Clockwork Monad's grinding perfection—a reminder that making is not just about the result, but about the joy of the act itself.
emphasizes: Creative Inspiration: the spark that begins every making
The Joy of Making: making as a celebration, not just a task
Ingenuity: finding new paths when old ones fail
Primal Craft: making as a fundamental, ancient act
Anima: breathing life into the things we create
Counterpoint to Perfection: embracing the beauty of the unfinished, the flawed, and the joyful

sample_adventure.title: The Forge That Would Not Cool
sample_adventure.description: A village forge has been burning for a week without fuel. The smith cannot stop working; his hands move even when he sleeps. The villagers believe he is cursed, but the Breath of the First Forge sees it differently—the smith has been touched by an excess of inspiration. The party must find a way to let the smith rest, and perhaps to remind the Breath that even the brightest spark needs to breathe.
sample_adventure.quote: Before the first hammer struck, there was the Breath. Before the last hammer falls, there will be silence. The silence is not an ending—it is a pause.
